JHB perfect electrical storm

By: Joy Summers | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
City power is in disarray and you as the resident are paying for it

Unique Selling Point:
Unique information (forensic report and sources and timing as rates are about to go up yet again

Summary:
Cable theft, mismanagement, excessive salaries and exorbitant rates - what is the state of city power and why does it matter. Without City power and the revenue from your electricity bills the city would collapse. Some believe its close to that already and now residents are having to fork out massive increases just to keep the lights on

Further information:
“ For every R1 owed to the City, the city expects only 20 cents will be collected. Electricity losses increased substantially to R3.43 billion, largely caused by R2.35 billion increase in non-technical electricity losses, which includes billing errors, bypassing and tampering of meters and illegal connections. The continued high allowance for impairment and electricity losses brings into doubt the viability of the city going forward. If the City does not arrest this trend, there will be a significant threat to the continued existence of the City in its current form.”

The City itself is under threat if these criminal trends and City Power inefficiency is not dramatically reversed.
The city have been blaming the cable thieves for its woes, but its only one small part of the puzzle. The absence of spending on infrastructure is another says Michael O Donovan – a data analyst and statistician. A former activist he has been documenting the numbers of Johannesburg for several years and his findings are startling.

Michael O Donovan’s study highlights how much more we are paying for so much less.
He will show Carte Blanche how Johannesburg residents now pay 150% more for power than they did ten years ago and it’s not just because of Eskom. The graphs that we will animate will show how city power have reduced their workforce but dramatically increased their salary bills. He also says that the city’s proposed budget that comes into effect in July is irrational, inflationary, arithmetically incoherent and demonstrates price gouging to the detriment of those the city is meant to serve.

Merritt Tyson

Mr. michael O donovan

Script:


City Powerless Final script for TX SUNDAY 22 May 2022

Commentary One
The city of Johannesburg is there to make the lives of its residents easier, but Freddie Nyathela has only ever seen the dark side of city officials

Freddie Nyathela
I could not believe my own people can treat us the way we were treated it was just unbelievable.

Commentary Two
Freddie’s fight centered around an incorrect bill for this building he had bought, for his non-profit organization- the South African Roadies association. A fight that has astonishingly continued for 17 long years

Freddie Nyathela
Can you imagine being charged R530 000 for one month for water?
Bongani
When you went in to the building what paying?
Freddie
R4000 but it just went crazy, crazy

Commentary Three
Freddie is a roadie- They’re the technical hot-shots that make musicians performances seamless. He wanted to give back those skills and train young South Africans- but he says the city thwarted him at every turn

Freddie
Its sheer abuse of power, at the expense of the African child
Bongani
And the city could never explain why your bill was so high
Freddie
No they could not.

Commentary Four
Freddie remembers every Johannesburg mayor for the last 17 years because none of them helped him. Neither did the City Ombudsman.

Freddie
We went through hell to put it bluntly

Commentary Five
In 2019 he took his fight to the public protector. Last month he was finally vindicated.
The Public protector found the city had violated the constitution and a raft of local legislation.


Bongani
But what did it say to you that it took what 17 years to get someone on your side?
Freddie
Eish! it’s a mixed feeling. This shouldn’t have happened

Commentary Six
In the 17 years that Freddie fought the city, Johannesburg rapidly declined.
Billing battles are common, and residents have become cash cows for administrations mired in corruption.

Up sound whoosh

Now the new multiparty coalition is trying to clean up Johannesburg. But they’re also asking its ratepayers for further increases

LINK
Just how deep is hole the City of Joburg finds itself in? Crumbling infrastructure, crime and grime, it feels a little unsafe just standing here under this bridge. Illegal connections- I mean the the list is endless.

Commentary seven
Michael O’ Donovan is a social scientist with a special interest in scraping and analyzing big data. He has looked at the latest increases and believes residents are being fleeced.

Bongani
Michael you are an ordinary member of the public why do you crunch these numbers, why do you do this work?
Michael
Probably outrage. We are being gouged, we are being taken advantage of

Commentary eight
O’ Donovan says the City of Johannesburg has lost sight of its purpose

Michael
The city appears to be acting as a self-interested, self-serving entity, it doesn’t appear to be acting as an entity that is there to serve the interests of the residents.

Commentary Nine
The proposed increases, he says of 9.61 % for electricity and 9.75% for water are higher than the actual cost of providing the service

Michael
The bulk service providers, Rand water, Eskom -set an increase, and we all know that those have been exorbitant over the last few years, and the city then goes and applies that to bulk purchases and all other costs, knowing full well that the other costs are not going up as much



Commentary Ten
But the city has a problem, many residents can no longer afford these increases. In June last year, Johannesburg’s own Municipal Finance Committee made a startling finding: For R1 00 they bill they expect to receive only 20 cents

Bongani
You think we have a broken city?
Michael
We have a broken city and the unfortunate part if the price increases that are being proposed result in less income, we are in a situation where the city may not be able to get out of this hole

Commentary Eleven
New Member of the Mayoral Committee Michael Sun, whose portfolio includes Pikitup, Johannesburg water and City Power says they are working night and day to revive the city, and keep rates affordable

Michael Sun
The city has to function, we buy water from Rand water, we buy electricity from Eskom so there is always a cost to the services we have to provide – if we had to always peg our increases on the inflation index, we most probably would not be able to bring services to the residents

Commentary Twelve
But with electricity bills increasing by 150% in ten years, it’s those costs that are really hurting residents

Link
Shock and horror - that’s my reaction to my monthly statement. Can you relate?
Look if it is indeed what we have consumed of course we should pay, but the question is, is City power a good custodian of our rands?

Commentary thirteen
Rene Kilner spends hours engaging City Power, because she helps businesses get accurate bills when many have given up, and has worked out the real costs of getting off the grid

Bongani
How reliable is the average household bill?
Rene
Probably 60% of them are incorrect
Bongani
And we are paying more than we owe?
Rene
Absolutely, yes

Commentary fourteen
In 2021 Rene reported City Power’s alleged license transgressions to NERSA

Rene
City Powers license should be taken away from them because they don’t comply not just from a metering point of view but from a safety point of view because they are actually putting people’s lives at risk

Commentary fifteen
Meyrick Ramatlo is acting for the acting CEO of City Power

Bongani
There are those who criticize the city and say that ultimately what it wants to do is try and use electricity as a cash cow?
Meyrick
Hey Bongani if you do a benchmark the tariff is still much lower compared to other municipalities

Commentary sixteen
But there’s more than one benchmark to judge City Power, another is their safety record. No one knows that better than Merritt Tyson. Shortly after he moved to Johannesburg, he got the shock of his life. Literally.

Zzzzz!!!

All his taps were live

Merritt
I just stepped in and touched the taps and it shocks you throughout the body

Commentary seventeen
But he was still determined to shower

Merritt
So I had to put on my slops so I wasn’t grounded, I had to go up to the tap turn it on, and then get into the shower with my slops, make sure I didn’t touch anything. Once I am finished leave the water running, get fully dry, change the slops, and then turn off the taps without touching the water. It was quite a mission to take a shower

Commentary eighteen
He couldn’t find the fault so he called an electrician

Merritt
And he thought something was weird, he started testing the gutters and the gutters were live. He was just testing things and everything was live


Commentary nineteen
Eventually the electrician traced the fault to City Power
Merritt
So he realized that City power live and earth had been connected the wrong way around to the house

Commentary twenty
But it still took a week for city power to arrive after the complaint was logged

Merritt
They said no we need to turn off your power until we can fix this because its fatal

Commentary Twenty one
So has City Power become a danger to its residents and a liability rather than an asset for Johannesburg?

Bongani
What is your response to the assertion that City Power is in a deep debt black hole
Meyrick Ramatlo
Look City Power is a going concern, I don’t agree with the assertion that we are there
Bongani
Meyrick the figure I have is a ten billion rand debt hole?
Merrick
For City Power we are talking of a figure R6 billion
Bongani
That is still significant?
Merrick
It’s very significant, it’s a concern for us
Bongani
Is City Power near collapse then?
Merrick
No its not, its still going concern. Our liabilities are at 70% of our assets

Commentary 22
But City Power’s six billion rand debt is just the start, more is needed to fix substations and infrastructure

Bongani
Are you spending enough on maintenance?
Merrick
We are spending enough on maintenance, but we have a backlog of about R26 billion basically to get the whole city infrastructure up and running, but instead its diverted in terms of dealing with replacement of cable theft, vandalized mini substations and the like

Commentary 23
R26 billion rand?! Even For MMC Sun that is a daunting figure



Michael Sun
When I received a report city power alone, has got a R26 billion infrastructure backlog then you will begin to understand the kind of challenges we face, not just in City Power but in the City of Johannesburg

Commentary 24
He now spends nights seeing first -hand how thieves are destroying City Powers infrastructure

Up sound
nothing here, nothing here, nothing

Michael Sun
It’s now developed into what I call cable robbery, it’s an entire syndicate at work

Commentary 25
But is the cable robbery a red herring?

Michael O’ Donovan
The theft of cables, substations pales into insignificance on the amount of money that is being spent on patchwork, piecemeal repairs to the infrastructure
Bongani
But the city will argue they have this infrastructure backlog that has been building up for two decades, they need money to fix it?
Michael
Well then where is the money going? If you look at City Power, capital investment is 1/ 6 of what it was in 2013. The number of employees in City Power is 1/3 of what it was.
Bongani
So they are paying more to fewer people to do less?
Michael
Yes.

Commentary 26
Disillusioned and angry residents are leaving the city. Others are considering off grid solutions

Rene
What the city is not realizing is that people might not be sitting on Carte Blanche talking about it, they are doing their talking in a very different way

Commentary 27
But now there are rumblings that the city may charge a solar tax.



Rene
The city says that they basically will penalize people who have gone off the grid or who are grid tied and have invested in alternative energy because they believe they are losing revenue

Commentary 28
But City power says there is no decision yet, and MMC Michael Sun assures residents that for the foreseeable future a solar tax is not part of the city’s plan

MMC Michael Sun
I think it’s a crazy idea. There certainly is no political direction from the executive mayor or myself to city power to say go and charge our residents a solar tax.

Commentary 29
City power is still the backbone of Johannesburg’s revenue. But its troubles threaten
the viability of the city itself, according to Johannesburg’s own public accounts committee. So we will have to pay up or Johannesburg as we know it could cease to exist - but is City Power keeping to its part of that social compact?

THE END 12 05

PROMO ONE
Johannesburg your rates are about to go up, and that means a higher electricity bill. But are you getting bang for your buck? And is City Power a good custodian of your rands

PROMO TWO
Commentary
City Power are facing multiple challenges but they’re confident they have the situation under control

Bongani
Meyrick the figure I have is a ten billion rand debt hole?
Merrick
For City Power it’s about R6 billion
Bongani
That is still significant?
Merrick
It’s very significant, it’s a concern for us
Bongani
Is City Power near collapse then?
Merrick
No its not





PROMO THREE
Freddie
I could not believe my own people can treat us the way we were treated.

Commentary
Billing chaos, crime and grime and exorbitant rates- Johannesburg residents are fed up
as another above inflation increase looms on the horizon

The absence of spending on infrastructure is another says Michael O Donovan – a data analyst and statistician. A former activist he has been documenting the numbers of Johannesburg for several years and his findings are startling. Michael O Donovan’s study highlights how much more we are paying for so much less. He will show Carte Blanche how Johannesburg residents now pay 150% more for power than they did ten years ago and it’s not just because of Eskom. The graphs that we will animate will show how city power have reduced their workforce but dramatically increased their salary bills.
